items.headline: Market Chatter: Lithium Miners' Profits Surge as Battery Storage Demand Drives Prices Higher
items.snippet: Lithium producers from China to Australia has seen profits soar as unrelenting demand from the energy storage sector pushes prices higher. US-headquartered Albemarle (ALB) noted that global lithium demand grew 45% through May this year, significantly outstripping supply.

items.headline: Albemarle's Lithium Math Turns Brutal
items.snippet: JPMorgan now expects lithium prices to remain in the low-$20-per-kilogram range, down from mid-$20s previously. Albemarle faces delays at the Greenbushes CGP3 plant following a June fire; the plant restarted Aug. 1. ALB shares were down 5.16% at $134.21 at the time of publication

items.headline: Albemarle to Benefit From Low-cost Assets, Brownfield Opportunity, RBC Says
items.snippet: RBC has an outperform rating on Albemarle and decreased the company's price target to $157 from $166, citing that while lithium prices have come off somewhat in Q2, the market remains somewhat tight and demand growth is outpacing added supply.

items.headline: Albemarle price target lowered to $161 from $189 at Morgan Stanley
items.snippet: Morgan Stanley analyst Vincent Andrews lowered the firm's price target on Albemarle to $161 from $189 and keeps an Equal Weight rating on the shares. Lithium prices have come off this cycle's peak, reducing the multiple assigned to Albemarle's lithium EBITDA.
